cells.tense: You're tending this now, and you know exactly how much it needs — no more, no less.
cells.ask: Let one finished thing stay finished, and let the letting-go be its own reward.
cells.core:
You're tending this now, and you know exactly how much it needs — no more, no less. Two things that both matter, and you're not choosing between them; you're giving each what it actually takes. That's harder than picking a side and you're doing it. You're not forcing anything forward and you're not letting anything starve — you're just there, day after day, keeping the conditions right.

A kitchen where something's rising and you're not opening the oven every five minutes — you set the conditions and you trust the time. What's yours now is the letting-go at the end: when the work is done, you get to feel it done. That's not quitting. That's the last part of the tending.
cells.sheetLine: You tend two things at once and don't force either.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady hands and a long view
cells.place: in the part of your life where you keep something alive while it grows

cells.tense: You're already tending a harvest that hasn't come in yet, bracing for what it'll need before it's asked.
cells.ask: Let one good thing you've actually made sit as finished before you dream the next one up.
cells.core:
You're already tending a harvest that hasn't come in yet, bracing for what it'll need before it's asked. You've moved past where this actually is and you're standing in a version ahead of it — watering, staking, planning for a yield that hasn't formed. The tending is real work. It's just aimed at a season that isn't here yet.

A garden where you're feeding the plant that's already grown and withholding from the one that's still sprouting — you've got the timing flipped. What's yours now is the satisfaction of a thing genuinely finished: when something you made is done, let it be done. The ease you're skipping is the fuel the next thing runs on.
cells.sheetLine: You're caring for the harvest before it's grown.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady hands and a long view
cells.place: in the part of your life where you keep something alive while it grows

cells.tense: You were the one who kept things alive, and somewhere along the way you stopped showing up for it.
cells.ask: Put one hand back on something small that's still growing and stay with it past the point where you'd usually drift.
cells.core:
You were the one who kept things alive, and somewhere along the way you stopped showing up for it. The care didn't leave — it's still there, watching — but the hands aren't in it. Nothing's being tended right now, and you're treating that as the truth about you instead of the state you're in.

A kitchen where the pot's still on the counter but the fire's gone out — everything's ready, nothing's moving. What's yours now is staying power: not a big return, one small stay. Pick the thing that's still within reach and tend it past the moment you'd normally walk away. What kept things alive before is still in you. It just needs to be used to come back.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending and called it who you are.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady hands and a long view
cells.place: in the part of your life where you keep something alive while it grows

cells.tense: You're already the one keeping this alive, and you talk about it like it's just how things run.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're tending that no one's thanked you for, out loud, to one person.
cells.core:
You're already the one keeping this alive, and you talk about it like it's just how things run. The tending is happening — you're the reason it's still going — but you've filed it under maintenance, under nobody's job in particular. The hands are yours. The story isn't.

A kitchen where the meal appears and no one asks who made it — you've been cooking so long you've stopped counting it as cooking. What's yours now is being seen as the one doing it, by you first. Not for credit. Because a thing you're carrying deserves to be named as carried, and the naming is the part you've been skipping.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending it and calling it nothing.
